A rough route is staged from Virginia Natural Gas's November 2019 project map. It is the route now filed under P5990, the VNG Interconnect, and moves to this row once the row exists.

Virginia Natural Gas filed for the Header Improvement Project with the State Corporation Commission on December 6, 2019, according to a Prince William Times article from December 2019. It was three new 30 inch pipelines, 24 miles in all, plus three compressor stations, at a cost of $346 million. It ran from Prince William County through Fauquier County and on to Hanover, New Kent and Charles City counties, mainly to supply the planned C4GT gas plant in Charles City County. The Commission dismissed the application on December 1, 2020, because the conditions it had set were not met. A Bay Journal article from December 2020 and Virginia Natural Gas's own press release both report this. The company then filed the smaller VNG Interconnect, which is a separate row (P5990). That project was withdrawn in 2021. The sheet had filed both projects as one row, with the Header Improvement Project's length, cost and route under the VNG Interconnect. Capacity for this project was not found, so none is entered. The route stays not mapped until the staged route is applied. Other names: the Chesapeake Climate Action Network page uses Header Injustice Project word for word, and the Bay Journal article uses HIP.
